label: rem:hadron-half-life-fermi
title: Fermi-constant relation, $q$-dependence, and parameter count
html:
Relation to the Fermi constant

Standard Fermi theory sets the decay rate as \Gamma = G_F^2m_e^5/(2\pi^3) \cdot |M|^2 \cdot f(Z, Q). This effective theory formula packages two distinct mass scales. The crossing energy is \mathfrak{E}_{\times} = \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}). The weak scale is v \approx 246 GeV, entering via G_F = 1/(\sqrt{2}v^2).

In the backup model m_e was read off the 3 crossings of the trefoil and v off the electroweak topology. In the corpus m_e is the CAL-1 leptonic mass-scale input, not derived from a knot (electron), so the ratio v / m_e \approx 4.8 \times 10^5 is not derived here.

The half-life depends on the combination

  G_F^2m_e^5
  = 
  \frac{m_e^5}{2v^4}
  = 
  \frac{(3\mathfrak{E}_{\times})^5}{2(N_v\mathfrak{E}_{\times})^4}
   \cdot  \mu_0
  = 
  \frac{243\mathfrak{E}_{\times}}{2N_v^4}
   \cdot  \mu_0,

with effective weak-scale crossing count N_v = v / (\mathfrak{E}_{\times}\mu_0). This reduces to a pure function of q times \mu_0: the Fermi constant is not an independent parameter.

q-dependence of the decay rate

The decay rate depends on q through four channels:

  • |\mathcal{W}(q)|^2: The T_{3,5} weak vertex form factor.
  • [2]_q = q + q^{-1}: The weak-vertex dimension.
  • |\mathcal{M}_q|^2: The Markov trace ratio. This reflects the crossing structure of the nuclear braid at q.
  • Q^5: The categorical action difference (transition energy). This depends on the pair Skein weights \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q), which depend on q through the dressed quark masses \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}, \mu_{\mathfrak{d}}. For q \neq 1, the q-anomaly \delta_q is nonzero and Q \neq T_e + T_{\nu^{\sigma}} + T_{\mathrm{recoil}}.

In the classical limit q = 1, s = 0 and [2]_1 = 2; crossing asymmetry vanishes, isobars become degenerate (Q = 0) and beta decay ceases. For q > 1, crossing asymmetry splits the isobars, yielding finite Q and finite half-lives.

Parameter count

The half-life formula depends on q (the substrate parameter, fixed by the muon-electron mass ratio), \mu_0 (a unit choice), and the nuclear quantum numbers (p, n). Every standard-physics constant decomposes into q-dependent factors times \mu_0: the electron mass is m_e = 3\mathfrak{E}_{\times}\mu_0, the weak scale is v = N_v\mathfrak{E}_{\times}\mu_0, and the fine structure constant is \alpha = q^{-1}/([9]_q \cdot [10]_q) (EM coupling projection), which is the bare form and sits -0.155\% from CODATA. The Chern-Simons correction is a separate and conjectural addition, stated in the Chern-Simons block rather than in the projection proposition, and its Gram constant \kappa is unproved; with the candidate \kappa at the proton-pinned q_0 it leaves -468\;\mathrm{ppb}.

Open computations

  1. Weak scale crossing count N_v. This must be derived (equivalently, v) from the Skein algebra. The T_{3,5} knot mediates the weak interaction, with the mass scale v emerging from the 10-crossing structure of the T_{3,5} braid: the vertex form factor \mathcal{W}(q) supplies the coupling and v provides the range.
  2. Weak vertex form factor \mathcal{W}_2(q) = t_1 + c_{\mathrm{em}}\,t_2, the two-term trace of (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5 (proof); its one-term part t_1 = \mathcal{W}(q) is the Markov trace in H_3(q). The charges on the three vertex strands and c_{\mathrm{em}} are not derived. What remains open is also its use: the half-life tables still carry the single-crossing approximation s^2, and whether replacing s^2 by |\mathcal{W}(q)|^2 resolves the systematic 10–17\% overshoot in heavy-nucleus half-life predictions has not been computed.
